--- package.json	
+++ package.json	
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+{
+  "name": "expand-range",
+  "version": "1.0.0",
+  "description": "Expand a range like '1-10' or 'a-z' into an array of all values in between.",
+  "type": "module",
+  "main": "src/expandRange.js",
+  "exports": "./src/expandRange.js",
+  "bin": {
+    "expand-range": "./bin/cli.js"
+  },
+  "files": [
+    "src",
+    "bin"
+  ],
+  "scripts": {
+    "test": "node --test"
+  },
+  "engines": {
+    "node": ">=18"
+  },
+  "license": "MIT"
+}

parts.text: Now the module. Let me write it carefully.

Wait, the test `'hello'` — does it match anything? CHAR_RANGE requires single char each side, so no. NUMERIC no. SINGLE no. So throws RangeError. Good.

`'1-'` — NUMERIC no (needs digits after). CHAR no. SINGLE no. throws. Good.

`''` — throws. Good.

Now run tests and CLI.

All tests pass. Project is set up. Let me mark todo complete.

Should I commit? No, user didn't ask. Let me give a concise summary.

All 11 tests pass and the CLI works.

```
/work
├── package.json          # ESM, zero deps, "test": "node --test"
├── .gitignore
├── src/expandRange.js    # expandRange() implementation
├── bin/cli.js            # expand-range <range...>
└── test/expandRange.test.js
```

`expandRange('1-10')` → `[1..10]`, `expandRange('a-z')` → `[a..z]`. Also handles descending (`5-1`), negatives (`-3-2`), single values (`5`/`c`), and rejects mixed-case or malformed input. Run with `npm test` or `node bin/cli.js 1-5 a-e`.
